children: CBOT grains are lower ahead of the long weekend, with the USDA and CBOT closed in observance of Labor Day on Monday. Traders are accounting for heightened risk for the long weekend including macro factors like wars in Russia versus Ukraine and U.S. versus Iran. They're also accounting for this afternoon's Commitment of Traders report from the USDA to show even higher net long positions in grain futures, particularly corn, says Doug Bergman of RCM Alternatives in a note. Most-active corn futures fall 0.2%, soybeans are down 0.1%, and wheat slides 1.8%. (kirk.maltais@wsj.com)
